events.title: Ptolemy IV defeats Antiochus III at the Battle of Raphia
events.description: Ptolemy IV Philopator of Egypt defeated the Seleucid king Antiochus III the Great near present-day Rafah in the Fourth Syrian War, with native Egyptian troops playing a significant role. The battle determined the sovereignty of Coele-Syria.
events.html: Ptolemy IV Philopator of Egypt defeated the Seleucid king Antiochus III the Great near present-day Rafah in the Fourth Syrian War, with native Egyptian troops playing a significant role. The battle determined the sovereignty of Coele-Syria.

events.title: Rome defeats Macedon at Pydna
events.description: Lucius Aemilius Paullus's legions broke the Macedonian phalanx of King Perseus. The Antigonid kingdom was abolished, and Rome became the dominant power in the Greek world.
events.html: Lucius Aemilius Paullus's legions broke the Macedonian phalanx of King Perseus. The Antigonid kingdom was abolished, and Rome became the dominant power in the Greek world.

events.title: Khan Krum routs the Byzantine army at Versinikia
events.description: Khan Krum of Bulgaria routed the Byzantine army of Emperor Michael I Rangabe near Versinikia, not far from Adrianople in Thrace. The defeat led to Michael's overthrow in favour of Leo V the Armenian, and Krum went on to besiege Adrianople.

events.title: Stephen IV is elected pope after the death of Leo III
events.description: Stephen IV, of a noble Roman family, was elected pope after the death of Pope Leo III earlier in June. In October he crowned Louis the Pious as emperor at Reims.
events.html: Stephen IV, of a noble Roman family, was elected pope after the death of Pope Leo III earlier in June. In October he crowned Louis the Pious as emperor at Reims.

events.title: Galileo is made to abjure before the Inquisition
events.description: Found 'vehemently suspect of heresy', Galileo formally abjured the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. He spent the rest of his life under house arrest.
events.html: Found 'vehemently suspect of heresy', Galileo formally abjured the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. He spent the rest of his life under house arrest.

events.title: Lord Mansfield rules in the Somerset case
events.description: The judge held that James Somerset, an enslaved man brought to England, could not be forcibly removed abroad. The ruling was widely taken to mean slavery had no basis in English law.
events.html: The judge held that James Somerset, an enslaved man brought to England, could not be forcibly removed abroad. The ruling was widely taken to mean slavery had no basis in English law.

events.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
events.description: Operation Barbarossa sent some three million Axis troops across a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The war in the east became the largest and deadliest land conflict in history.
events.html: Operation Barbarossa sent some three million Axis troops across a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The war in the east became the largest and deadliest land conflict in history.

events.title: Roosevelt signs the G.I. Bill
events.description: The Servicemen's Readjustment Act gave veterans college tuition, low-cost home loans and unemployment pay. Millions took up its benefits, expanding higher education and home ownership.
